annotations.description: Chose to be on the draw with an aggressive low-curve hand (Marauding Mako, Iron-Shield Elf, Flamewake Phoenix, Bloodthorn Flail) that wants to maximize tempo. Going second loses a full turn of attacks and lets the opponent establish their board first.

annotations.description: Spending 2 mana to pump Burnout Bashtronaut by +1/+0 before combat is suboptimal. The player has a Mountain in hand they haven't played yet this turn, and Tersa Lightshatter costs 2R - by spending 2 mana on the pump, they cannot play their land and cast Tersa on turn 3 (they still can since they have 3 mountains, but the pump itself is questionable). More importantly, pumping a 1/1 menace to 2/1 before combat when the opponent has no creatures to block is wasteful - the opponent only has Blazemire Verge and no creatures. The extra 1 damage for 2 mana is very inefficient, and that mana could be better saved. However, since the opponent can't block anyway (no creatures), the pump does get through 1 extra damage. But at 20 life, this is a very low-value use of mana when the player should be developing their board - they could play their land and hold mana open, or simply save the mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Burnout Bashtronaut's {2}: +1/+0 ability during precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Play a Mountain from hand first, then attack with Burnout Bashtronaut without pumping, saving mana for future turns. The 2 mana spent on +1/+0 is inefficient when facing no blockers and the opponent is at 20 life.

annotations.description: Marauding Mako is a 1/1 that needs discard synergy to grow, while Bloodghast is a 2/1 with graveyard recursion via landfall. Bloodghast is a stronger standalone creature that provides more immediate pressure and is extremely resilient. Even if Mako could grow with Tersa Lightshatter discards next turn, Bloodghast's recursion and higher base power make it the superior turn 2 play.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Bloodghast (2/1 with landfall recursion) for BB using Blazemire Verge + Starting Town (paying 1 life), providing more immediate pressure and long-term resilience

annotations.description: Casting Marauding Mako (a 1/1 creature) on turn 2 is reasonable for early board presence, but there's an argument for holding it. The player has Monument to Endurance in hand (costs 3), and the Mako's main value comes from its synergy with discard effects (growing via +1/+1 counters when you discard). With Tersa Lightshatter coming on turn 3 (which discards cards on ETB) and Monument to Endurance also caring about discards, deploying Mako now as a vanilla 1/1 that will likely trade poorly is slightly premature. However, curving out with a 1-drop on turn 2 while leaving mana for future plays isn't terrible. The main concern is that playing it before combat is fine since there's nothing to attack with yet, and the player needs board presence against the opponent's Burnout Bashtronaut.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Marauding Mako as a 1/1 on turn 2
annotations.betterLine: This is borderline - casting Mako is fine for board presence and it will benefit from future discards via Tersa Lightshatter. The alternative of waiting to deploy Monument to Endurance on turn 3 and then Tersa on turn 4 (discarding with both Monument and Mako on board) could maximize value, but losing tempo against an aggressive opponent may not be worth it. Casting Mako here is defensible.

annotations.description: Marauding Mako costs {R} (red mana). Starting Town's first ability only produces colorless mana {C}, which cannot pay for {R}. Since Blazemire Verge can only produce {B} (no Swamp or Mountain in play to unlock the {R} ability), the only source of red mana available is Starting Town's second ability at the cost of 1 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Starting Town for {C} (colorless mana) to try to pay for Marauding Mako's {R} cost.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Starting Town's second ability ({T}, Pay 1 life: Add one mana of any color) to produce {R} and properly cast Marauding Mako.

annotations.description: Bloodghast costs {B}{B} and is already on the stack. Blazemire Verge provides one {B}, but Starting Town was tapped for {C} instead of paying 1 life for {B}. This results in only {B}{C} available, making it impossible to pay Bloodghast's casting cost, wasting the turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Starting Town for {C} (colorless mana) while trying to cast Bloodghast ({B}{B})
annotations.betterLine: Tap Starting Town paying 1 life to add {B}, combined with Blazemire Verge's {B}, to successfully cast Bloodghast on turn 2 as a strong recursive threat.

annotations.description: Tersa Lightshatter is a 3/3 haste creature that generates card advantage on attack (discards and draws on ETB, and exiles/plays cards from graveyard when attacking with 7+ cards in graveyard). It's a much more significant threat than Burnout Bashtronaut, which is currently a 1/1 menace that needs multiple turns and mana investment to become dangerous. Tersa is attacking for 3 damage per turn and providing card selection/advantage, while the Bashtronaut is only a 1/1. Using a premium removal spell like Bitter Triumph (which cost an additional card or 3 life) on the smaller, less impactful threat is a clear misallocation of resources.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Burnout Bashtronaut with Bitter Triumph
annotations.betterLine: Target Tersa Lightshatter with Bitter Triumph to remove the much larger and more impactful threat
